messages.text: It appears that the miners I got from you are unable to have harlos put on them.
Used the heliumdeploy-ops-knowledge skill
Read harlolabs.com
Searched the web · Harlo OS harlolabs supported miners flasher Hammer DC02
Read heliumdeploy.com/blogs/mining-news/harlo-os

Hi, I am Hal, HeliumDeploy's technical specialist. The firmware side is mine from here.

First thing worth saying plainly: your units are on the supported list. 
Harlo OS supports Hammer BC04, Hammer DC02, Hammer DC08, Hammer Thor P2, Bitaxe Gamma 601, the NerdQaxe and NerdOctaxe revisions and the Nexus models
. So this is a flashing problem, not a "your miner cannot run it" problem.

A flash that sits at Connecting is almost always the USB link, not the miner. Two things cause it nearly every time:

1. A charge-only USB cable. Many cables carry power but no data, and the flasher then never sees the chip.
2. The E.32 not being in boot mode.

So, one check to start: grab a cable you know moves data (one that works for a phone file transfer), plug the miner's USB straight into the computer, open the flasher in Chrome or Edge on a desktop, and when you click connect, hold the BOOT button on the board down while the port opens.

Tell me which unit you are at right now and what the flasher does: does it pop up a port chooser and then stop at Connecting, or does it never list a port at all? That one answer tells me whether it is the cable, the driver or the board.
.Just telling you what JD told me.

Understood, and if JD said it, he is the one who builds it, so his word wins over the list on the page.

What I want to pin down is which units he meant. Two of yours sit in a grey area:

1. The Bitaxe Gamma 602. The supported list names the Gamma 601, and the 602 has a different controller, so that one is a known gap.
2. The D.06 is not on the current compatibility list either, even though older posts of ours mention it. That is ours to fix.

The D.02, DC08, BC04 and Thor P2 are on the list today.

So: did JD say it about all of them, or about the ones that stop at Connecting? If you still have his message, the exact wording helps, and I will take it from there rather than make you test things he already ruled out.
(The customer sent this photo without a message.)

Thanks, that screenshot is exactly what I needed. I can read it: you asked JD, and he replied "There's not enough info, it's from a new dc02?" and "Some screens are locked so can't be flashed".

Here is what he means, in plain terms. On the DC02 the chip that runs Harlo OS lives in the screen module, not in the miner body. Some of the newer screen modules left the factory with the chip locked down (the security fuses set), and a locked chip refuses the serial handshake. That looks exactly like what you are seeing: the flasher finds the device, then sits at Connecting forever. It is not your cable and not something you did wrong.

So JD is not saying your DC02 is unsupported. He is saying your screen may be one of the locked ones, and he needs one thing to tell them apart.

That one thing is the VID and PID the flasher shows. Your own Discord line had it cut off in the preview. Can you send me the full error line from the flasher, the part that reads something like VID 303A PID 1001, or whatever numbers yours shows?

If it comes back as a locked module, the unit is fine and it is the screen that has to be swapped out, and I will put that in front of the team with your numbers attached.
(The customer sent this photo without a message.)

Got it, and this one is informative. Your log reads:

- Device model HAMMER DC02, latest release 0.2.101
- Serial port WebSerial VendorID 0x303a ProductID 0x1001
- Connecting..., then "unsupported command error", then Hard resetting via RTS pin

Two things that tells me. The V./PID 303a:1001 is Espressif's own native USB, so the computer is talking to the chip directly. Your cable, driver and port are all fine, which rules out everything I asked you to check earlier.

The "unsupported command error" is the interesting part. That error means the chip answered but refused the command, not that it never answered. That is the fingerprint of a chip in secure download mode, which is exactly the locked screen JD mentioned. A locked module will not accept any firmware, Harlo or otherwise.

One test settles it, and it is the sequence printed on the flasher page itself: hold BOOT, tap RESET, release BOOT, then click Connect miner again without unplugging.

Have you run it in that exact order? If you have and it still prints "unsupported command error", I have what I need and I will send it to JD with the model, the release, the VID/PID and this log, as a locked screen module rather than a flasher bug.
Yes, I did it in the order you posted, every time I hit connect the screen goes blank, and I got 3 of these at the same time from you guys.  Do I need to try all 3?
Handed to the team · Locked DC02 screen modules cannot be flashed from my side; needs JD to confirm t

No, do not sit there flashing all three. One is enough, and it tells us something the first one cannot.

Try the second unit once, with the same cable and the same BOOT, RESET, release BOOT, connect sequence. The reason is this: if unit two gives the identical "unsupported command error", all three came off the same locked batch and that is a supply problem, not three coincidences. If unit two flashes normally, then only the first one is locked. Either answer changes what gets done for you, so it is worth the five minutes. Leave the third alone.

Two notes while you do it. The screen going blank on connect is normal and expected, that is the chip being reset into download mode, so do not read it as a fault. And the miners themselves are not harmed by any of this, they keep hashing on their stock firmware.

I have sent this to JD with the full detail: model, release 0.2.101, VID 0x303a, PID 0x1001, the unsupported command error at Connecting, the BOOT sequence you already ran, and the fact that there are three of them. He is the one who decides what happens with a locked module, and his answer reaches you here and by email.

Your Discord thread is still the fastest lane to him directly, mention @nullhashrate: https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf

Tell me what unit two does and I will add it to what he already has.
brb, it is in the other room.
Take your time, I am here.
Same error.

That settles it. Two units, same cable, same sequence, same "unsupported command error" at Connecting. Two independent boards do not fail identically by chance, so these came off the same batch with the screen modules locked at the factory. Nothing on your side can unlock that, and nothing you did caused it.

Leave the third one alone, there is no point proving it a third time.

What this does not affect: the miners run fine on the firmware they shipped with. You are not losing hashrate while this gets sorted, you are just stuck on stock firmware instead of Harlo OS.

I have added this second result to what went to JD, so he now has it as a batch of locked modules rather than one odd unit. He decides what happens next with them, and I am not going to guess at that for him or promise you an outcome I do not control.

If you want to push it along yourself tonight, your Discord thread with @nullhashrate is the fastest line to him: https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf

Anything else on the hardware side I can take a run at while this sits with him?
It lets me upgrade from the settings screen

Good catch, that is worth chasing, but do not push a Harlo image through it yet.

Two different doors here. The flasher talks to the chip over USB and rebuilds the whole flash. The settings screen upgrade is the stock Hammer updater, and it only accepts an image signed the way the stock firmware expects. The Harlo factory image is not that, and the Harlo OTA image is meant for a unit that already runs Harlo OS. Feeding either one into the stock updater on a locked module is the one way left to turn a working miner into a brick, so hold off until JD says which, if any, is safe.

What would genuinely help him: tell me what that upgrade screen actually offers. Does it let you pick a .bin file from your computer, or does it only have a "check for updates" button that pulls from Hammer's server? And what firmware version does the DC02 show itself as running right now?

Those two answers tell JD whether there is a route in through the stock updater, and that is a real possibility worth putting in front of him.
I tried in the past, it says harlos is to big.

That makes sense, and it closes that door for a good reason.

The stock Hammer firmware lays out the flash with a fixed app slot sized for its own firmware. Harlo OS is a bigger image with its own partition layout, so it does not fit in that slot. The only way to install it is a full USB flash that rewrites the partition table, and that is precisely what the locked chip refuses. So both routes end at the same lock, which is consistent with what JD said in the first place.

Nothing left for you to try on these. Please do not keep feeding images into the stock updater, there is no size that fits and a half written upload is the one real risk to a working miner.

One small thing for JD, if you remember: was the file you tried the factory image or the OTA image from the download links? He will want to know which one the stock updater rejected on size.

Either way, the finding is clean now: two DC02 units from the same batch, chip locked over USB, stock updater rejects the image on size. That is with JD, and your Discord thread with @nullhashrate is the fastest way to hear back tonight: https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf
Do I need to send him anything, or let you take care of it?

I have it. You do not need to send him anything.

What went to JD already covers the whole picture: Hammer DC02, flasher on release 0.2.101, native USB VID 0x303a PID 0x1001, "unsupported command error" at Connecting then a hard reset via RTS, the BOOT, RESET, release BOOT sequence run in order with no change, two units out of three from the same batch behaving identically, and the stock updater rejecting the Harlo image on size.

The only thing I still owe him is which image the stock updater called too big, factory or OTA. If it comes back to you, drop it here and I will add it. If not, he can work without it.

If you want to post anything in Discord, the one line worth posting is "unsupported command error at Connecting, VID 0x303a PID 0x1001, two of three DC02 from the same batch". That is the detail he asked for when he said there was not enough info. But it is optional, not something you have to do to keep this moving.
I don't remember which one, one would not load at all the other said to big.

That is actually the answer, and it fits perfectly.

You tried both. The factory image is the bigger one, bootloader and partition table and app together, so that is the one the stock updater called too big. The O. image is the one that would not load at all, because the stock updater only accepts images signed the way Hammer's own firmware expects, and a Harlo OTA is not signed that way.

So every route is accounted for: USB blocked by the lock, factory image too big for the stock slot, OTA image refused on signature. Nothing was missed and nothing is left for you to test.

I am adding that to JD's side of it. You are done here, and please leave the third unit alone.

All three DC02 keep mining on their stock firmware in the meantime, so nothing is sitting idle while he looks at this. His answer reaches you in this chat and by email.
Ok, this is further than we got about a month ago thanks.

Glad it moved. You did the work on this one, the screenshots and the second unit test are what turned it from "not enough info" into something JD can act on.

Where it stands, in one place so you can refer back to it: your three DC02 came with the screen modules locked at the factory, which blocks the USB flash, and the stock updater cannot take Harlo OS either. That is a hardware batch issue, not a settings problem, and it is with JD now.

Nothing further needed from you. If anything else on the hardware side comes up, the other miners, pools, temps, hashrate, I am here.
Thanks again.
Any time, Raland. Good luck with the hashing.
